hypotheses.claim: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms, a ruin priority that multiplies normalized removal savings by tight-capacity load relief (demand/route_load) and by within-route geographic compactness, with a stagnation_ratio- and iter_frac-driven decay of the savings term, will lower mean objective below the current SBS 15.7435 — because the portfolio's residual VBS gap (0.43%) and all five weakest regimes sit on tight-capacity, clustered, size-100 instances where pure savings ranking repeatedly removes the same long-detour nodes and leaves infeasible-ish, load-imbalanced routes for Regret-2 to repair.

next_search_advice.direction: Sharpen the ruin-selection priority hook for the documented weakest regimes (tight capacity, uniform demand, size 100, eccentric depot, clustered spatial): replace the current removal-savings-only ranking with a scale-invariant multiplicative blend of (a) per-node removal savings normalized by mean savings, (b) load-relief pressure (removed demand / route load, which matters most at tight capacity), and (c) Shaw-style geographic relatedness to the seed node's route centroid (clustered spatial), then anneal that blend toward a milder, stagnation-driven schedule as iter_frac grows so late LNS iterations explore rather than re-destroy the same high-savings nodes.
